scope: California outer coast. These five CDFW ocean/groundfish planning regions are not the jurisdiction boundaries for every species. San Francisco Bay requires its own rules.

policy.promotion: Two independent, dated, geographically located observations within 14 days support a regional report flag. Port totals without fishing coordinates do not. ENSO alone never promotes a target, assigns catch probability or opens a season. New target definitions require biological and regulatory review.

regions.name: Northern
regions.note: Cold-water reef and shelf fisheries; Pacific halibut is distinct from California halibut. Salmon and crab remain subject to local seasons and closures.

target_options.name: Lingcod & rockfish
target_options.note: Rocky habitat and vegetation with prey support an adult search; ledges and crevices have a seasonal spawning role. Juvenile sandy habitat cannot be substituted for the adult target. Rocky reefs host many rockfish, but species differ in habitat and height above bottom. The shared selector is a fishing convenience, not a single biological niche.

target_options.name: Pacific halibut
target_options.note: A northern shelf flatfish, distinct from California halibut. Look for sediment habitat and shelf relief; this directory has no depth-qualified grounds for it.

target_options.name: Chinook salmon
target_options.note: Migratory ocean fish follow changing prey and ocean conditions. NOAA reports anchovies dominating Central Coast ocean-caught Chinook diets in 2020–2021; that dated finding does not locate a current school.

target_options.name: Dungeness crab
target_options.note: CDFW quality sampling uses depth strings at 90, 150–180 and 210–240 feet. Those are sampling strata, not proof that the deepest stratum maximizes recreational catch.

target_options.name: Albacore tuna
target_options.note: Ocean temperature and frontal structure influence albacore distribution. NOAA describes broad migrations; a suitable water mass does not establish fish presence.

target_options.name: California halibut
target_options.note: California halibut use soft-bottom inner-shelf and estuarine habitat. CDFW describes most angler catches in shallow water; this does not establish a universal optimum at every port.

watch_options.name: Pacific bluefin tuna
watch_options.note: Pacific bluefin occupy a broad range and migrate over large distances. Feeding, body size and depth behavior make a single fixed surface-temperature optimum inappropriate.

regions.note: Exposed rocky coast and offshore shelf. Pacific halibut rules change at Point Arena; offshore albacore opportunity depends on the actual water mass and forage.

watch_options.name: California yellowtail
watch_options.note: NOAA describes yellowtail as mobile predators of small schooling fish and squid; movements into California vary with seasonal ocean conditions.

watch_options.name: Yellowfin tuna
watch_options.note: NOAA describes yellowfin as tropical/subtropical migratory fish that also occur off Southern California; distribution and depth use change with conditions and life stage.

watch_options.name: Dorado · dolphinfish
watch_options.note: Pacific dorado use warm upper-ocean habitat and can associate with floating material. These moving features cannot support permanent catch coordinates.

regions.name: Southern
regions.note: Kelp bass, yellowtail, seabass, tuna and spiny lobster lead the southern selection. Lingcod occur here, but the reef selector is called Rockfish; separate species limits still apply.

target_options.name: Kelp bass · calico
target_options.note: CDFW describes adult kelp bass in nearshore reef and kelp habitat and the recreational fishery mainly on shallow reefs and kelp beds to about 70 ft.

target_options.name: California yellowtail
target_options.note: NOAA describes yellowtail as mobile predators of small schooling fish and squid; movements into California vary with seasonal ocean conditions.

target_options.name: White seabass
target_options.note: CDFW describes adults along kelp margins, rocky headlands and offshore waters around Southern California and the islands. Their movement prevents a fixed habitat patch from guaranteeing presence.

target_options.name: Barred sand bass
target_options.note: Adults use sand or mud near structure and can aggregate over soft bottom seasonally. Southern California telemetry supports the importance of sand–reef interfaces.

target_options.name: Spotted sand bass
target_options.empty_map_note: Bay / estuary habitat not mapped here yet. Island reefs are not spotted sand bass grounds.
target_options.note: CDFW describes spotted sand bass as strongly associated with bays and estuaries, with limited exchange among many local populations.

target_options.name: Pacific bonito
target_options.empty_map_note: Mobile coastal schools: no current fish sightings or fixed grounds mapped.
target_options.note: CDFW describes Pacific bonito as mobile upper-water schools found in coastal, island and offshore habitat; historical catch patterns vary with ocean conditions.

target_options.name: California barracuda
target_options.empty_map_note: Mobile coastal schools: dated kelp is context only; no current fish sightings mapped.
target_options.note: CDFW describes California barracuda schooling near the surface and feeding on small fish; Southern California recreational encounters are seasonally variable.

target_options.name: California sheephead
target_options.note: Rocky reef and kelp habitat support sheephead. Their female-to-male life history makes size and sex structure ecologically important.

target_options.name: Ocean whitefish
target_options.note: Ocean whitefish use the water above rocky and mixed-bottom habitat. A historical Channel Islands synthesis describes islands and banks as important habitat.

target_options.name: California spiny lobster
target_options.note: Channel Islands spiny lobster use rocky shelter and kelp habitat. Reef cavities provide habitat context but a coarse bathymetric grid cannot resolve individual dens.
